chief_complaint: Management of type 2 diabetes mellitus with chronic kidney disease and metabolic syndrome
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58‑year‑old Asian male with a long history of type 2 diabetes diagnosed in 2005, complicated by progressive diabetic kidney disease (CKD stages 1 and 2) and micro‑albuminuria noted since 2010. Metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, obesity (BMI ≥ 30) and obstructive sleep apnea have been present for over a decade. Anemia has been chronic since the late 1980s. Recent laboratory data show a very low hemoglobin A1c of 3.8% despite ongoing insulin therapy, raising concern for overtreatment or laboratory error. Blood pressure is recorded as 114/82 mmHg but is flagged as stage 1 hypertension. The medication list contains only insulin, with no antihypertensive, lipid‑lowering, or renal‑protective agents. A medication review was triggered on 2025‑06‑28. Socially, the patient is employed full‑time, has higher education, a criminal record, and reports intimate‑partner abuse, all of which may affect adherence and overall health.
